evidence.field: file description; original image link; licensing
evidence.text: The exact file page identifies 干-seal.svg as a vector depiction of 干 in Shuowen seal-script style, links its original SVG, and attributes the drawing to a modern contributor. It cites Hanziyuan image s01611 as its picture source. The page declares the vector representation public domain; attribution is appreciated but not required. This is a modern redraw of a received seal-style form, not an ancient artifact image.
evidence.title: File:干-seal.svg — Wikimedia Commons

evidence.text: The article reports the earliest securely identifiable 干 in its account on a mid-Western Zhou 豦簋 inscription. It describes later Western Zhou and subsequent form changes, while treating proposed earlier Shang identifications as debated. This supports using the Commons seal redraw only to illustrate a later received form, not to establish the graph's earliest origin or a full lineage.

search_audit.query: 干 seal form Wikimedia Commons干-seal.svg Shuowen received seal script
search_audit.outcome: Opened the exact 干-seal.svg Commons description page and inspected its stated identity, source attribution, original-file link, and public-domain terms; also inspected the NTU paleographic article on dating and graphic changes. The alternate Shuowen Seal Radical 047.svg description page failed with a cache miss. Following the Commons original-file link returned an SVG content-type error, but the exact page supplied its direct original SVG link.
Search results confirmed the exact file page and its Shuowen seal-script description; selection and rights rely on the opened description page.

gaps: The chosen Commons image is a modern redraw and no pixel-level visual inspection was performed in this research pass. Its use should be captioned as a received Shuowen seal-style form, not an artifact photograph or proof of early origin.

The numbered alternate seal file's page could not be opened, so its identity, original image URL, provenance, and reuse rights remain unverified. No Xiaoxuetang image was selected or investigated in this focused pass.

limitations.text: This modern redraw illustrates the received seal-style form only. It is not a dated artifact image and cannot establish the shield interpretation, earliest attestation, or a complete graphic lineage.
